metadata.title: Flexible Weekly Meal Prep Plan
metadata.purpose: Seed data and build brief for a web interface for grocery planning, flexible meal prep, weekly meal pools, recipes, and vegetable prep guidance.

codex_build_brief.app_goal: Build a web interface that lets the user access a flexible weekly meal prep system with grocery lists, prep-day options, meal pools, recipes, and gut-friendly vegetable prep instructions.
codex_build_brief.important_note: This should not be a rigid fixed meal plan. The interface should let the user choose optional meal-prep combinations based on mood while still minimizing grocery time and ingredient overlap.

suggested_pages.title: Grocery List
suggested_pages.purpose: Show Saturday main grocery and Tuesday refresh grocery, grouped by ingredient family, with checkboxes.

suggested_pages.title: Meal Prep Plan
suggested_pages.purpose: Show flexible Saturday and Tuesday prep frameworks with optional prep combinations.

suggested_pages.title: Flexible Weekly Menu
suggested_pages.purpose: Show day-by-day meal option pools instead of one rigid menu.

suggested_pages.title: Recipes
suggested_pages.purpose: Alphabetical recipe index with detail pages and slugs.

suggested_pages.title: Vegetable Prep Guide
suggested_pages.purpose: Roasting, steaming, sautéing, gut-friendly bowl ratios, and storage rules.

recommended_features: Search recipes, grocery items, and prep tasks.
Checkbox mode for grocery shopping and prep steps.
Filter recipes by cuisine, meal type, batch, dairy-free, no-maida, quick breakfast, gut-friendly.
Meal pool UI: Saturday batch meals and Tuesday batch meals.
Allow selecting a weekly prep mode: Light Week, Comfort Week, Curry Week, Balanced Week.
Generate grocery list based on selected prep mode.
Link weekly meal option names to recipe pages using recipe slugs.
Mobile-friendly layout for grocery shopping and kitchen use.
Print-friendly export for grocery list and prep checklist.

health_context: Facial acne; dairy and sugar tend to show up on face.
Occasional bowel movement issues and constipation, sometimes leading to piles.
Regularly takes iron, vitamin D, and omega-3 supplements.
avoid_or_minimize: Paneer as a regular weekly protein; keep paneer optional/occasional
Too much onion/garlic if bloating occurs
preferred_variety: South Indian: sambar rice, idli, coconut chutney
Flexible pyaaz-tamatar-garlic gravy base for tofu/chana/mixed vegetables
supplement_and_absorption_notes: Take iron away from tea/coffee and calcium-heavy foods.
Use lemon/lime or other vitamin C foods with iron-rich plant meals.

weekly_constraints.breakfast_constraint: Leaves home by 7 AM most days, so breakfast should be quick/no-cook except Tuesday when working from home.
weekly_constraints.white_rice_note: White rice is acceptable instead of brown rice. Keep portions moderate and pair with dal/tofu/chana, cooked vegetables, greens, seeds, and lemon/lime.

planning_principles: Use a flexible prep framework, not a rigid fixed menu.
Each prep day should create building blocks that can become multiple meals.
Cluster similar-ingredient dishes by grocery day to reduce shopping time and waste.
Cooked/roasted vegetables should be the main vegetable base for bowls; raw vegetables should be toppings.
Keep grains, proteins, cooked vegetables, greens, and sauces separate.
Do not prep every possible dish every week; choose 1–2 mains plus supporting components.
Saturday focuses on Indian + Mediterranean + Mexican + optional pav bhaji/gravy.
Tuesday focuses on South Indian + Thai + fresh produce reset.
Use tofu as the default flexible protein; paneer only as an occasional optional swap.

Saturday.theme: Indian + Mediterranean + Mexican + optional pav bhaji/gravy
Saturday.rule: Choose 1–2 mains only, plus supporting building blocks. Do not cook every possible option.
formula: 1 Indian comfort main: spinach moong dal OR high-veg pav bhaji OR gravy-based tofu/chana
1 protein/bean: chickpeas, kala chana, tofu, or black beans
1 vegetable batch: roasted vegetables OR pav bhaji vegetables
1 fresh bowl base: lettuce, cucumber, microgreens
1–2 sauces: tahini dressing, salsa, mint chutney, or gravy base

options.name: Comfort Week

options.name: Curry Week

options.name: Balanced Week

Saturday.recommended_default: Balanced Week: small spinach moong dal + small high-veg pav bhaji, plus white rice, greens, and one sauce.

Tuesday.theme: South Indian + Thai + optional gravy refresh
Tuesday.rule: Use Tuesday as a freshness reset. Choose 1 South Indian base + 1 protein/vegetable option + 1 sauce/chutney.
formula: 1 South Indian main: sambar OR rasam-style dal
1 protein: tofu cubes OR tofu curry
1 side vegetable: bhindi, cabbage poriyal, or broccoli
1 breakfast item: idli or oats jars
1 sauce/chutney: coconut chutney or peanut sauce
Fresh refresh: lettuce, cucumber, herbs, microgreens

vegetable_prep_guide.recommendation: For this gut pattern, use cooked/roasted vegetables as the main base and raw vegetables as toppings. Large raw salads may worsen bloating.

method_comparison.best_for: Broccoli, cauliflower, carrots, bell peppers, zucchini, pumpkin
Broccoli, green beans, carrots, cauliflower, pumpkin
Cucumber, lettuce, microgreens, small cabbage amount

steps: Preheat oven to 400°F / 200°C.
Wash vegetables and dry very well.
Cut into medium-sized pieces; avoid tiny pieces because they get mushy.
Toss with oil and spices.
Spread on baking tray in a single layer; do not overcrowd.
Roast 20–30 minutes, flipping once halfway.
Roast to about 80–85% cooked for meal prep, not fully mushy.
Cool completely before storing.
roasting.add_later: Add lemon/lime, tahini dressing, salsa, or peanut sauce when eating, not before storing.

steps: Boil water in a pot.
Place vegetables in steamer basket.
Cover and steam until just tender, not mushy.
Spread on plate/tray to cool and release steam.
Store only after fully cool and dry.
Season lightly when eating.

cabbage_poriyal_steps: Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, curry leaves, and hing.
Cook on medium until soft but not mushy.
Add optional 1–2 tbsp coconut at the end.
bhindi_sabzi_steps: Add bhindi and cook uncovered on medium.
Add turmeric, coriander powder, salt once bhindi starts cooking down.
Add amchur or lemon at the end.

storage_rules: Cool cooked vegetables completely before closing lid.
Do not mix cucumber/tomato into cooked vegetables in advance.
Use a clean spoon every time.
Reheat only the portion you eat.

recipes.name: Besan Chilla with Mint-Cilantro Chutney
recipes.best_for: Tuesday work-from-home breakfast, light dinner, or high-protein snack.
steps: Mix besan, turmeric, cumin, ajwain, hing, and salt.
Add water slowly and whisk into smooth pourable batter.
Add carrot, spinach/methi, onion, and cilantro.
Rest 5–10 minutes if possible.
Cook on a lightly greased nonstick pan like a thin pancake.
Blend chutney ingredients with enough water until smooth.
Serve hot with chutney.
meal_prep_notes: Batter can be refrigerated up to 1 day.
health_notes: Dairy-free, no maida, no added sugar.
Ajwain, hing, ginger, and mint are digestion-friendly.

recipes.name: Gravy-Based Tofu/Chana Bowl
recipes.best_for: A flexible Indian bowl when pyaaz-tamatar-garlic gravy is prepped.

Main.item: Roasted vegetables or cooked mixed vegetables

steps: Warm rice.
Warm tofu or chana with gravy.
Add roasted or cooked vegetables if desired.
Serve as a bowl with cucumber/microgreens on the side.
Add lemon before eating.
meal_prep_notes: Use tofu most often; use chana if tolerated.
Paneer can be an occasional swap, not default.
health_notes: Watch onion/garlic quantity if bloating occurs.
Tofu is preferred over paneer for acne-friendly routine.

recipes.name: High-Veg Pav Bhaji with Whole Grain Toast/Roti
recipes.best_for: Comfort meal variation without relying on dairy or maida.

Serve With.item: Whole grain toast, sourdough, whole wheat bun, or roti

steps: Boil or pressure cook potatoes, cauliflower, carrots, peas, and optional lauki/cabbage until soft.
Heat oil or small amount of vegan butter.
Cook onion until soft, then add ginger-garlic.
Add tomatoes, turmeric, pav bhaji masala, and salt.
Cook until tomatoes break down.
Add cooked vegetables and mash well.
Simmer 10–15 minutes, adding water as needed.
Finish with lemon and cilantro.
Serve with whole grain toast/roti instead of regular maida pav.
meal_prep_notes: Use small potato amount and more vegetables.
health_notes: Comfort food without dairy/maida if served correctly.
Can be heavy if too much potato, butter, or regular pav is used.

recipes.name: Idli with Sambar and Coconut Chutney
recipes.best_for: Fast breakfast, light dinner, or South Indian comfort meal.
recipes.servings: 2 meals if using 6–8 idlis and 3–4 cups sambar
steps: Pressure cook toor dal with turmeric until very soft and mash lightly.
Cook chopped sambar vegetables until soft.
Add dal, tamarind, sambar powder, salt, and water; simmer 10–15 minutes.
Temper mustard seeds, cumin, curry leaves, hing, and ginger; add to sambar.
Steam idlis 10–12 minutes.
Blend coconut chutney ingredients.
Serve idli with sambar and 2–3 tbsp chutney.
meal_prep_notes: Idli keeps 2–3 days in fridge or can be frozen.
Coconut chutney is best within 1–2 days.

recipes.name: Mediterranean Chickpea Quinoa Bowl
recipes.best_for: Sunday lunch or Monday dinner.
steps: Add quinoa, chickpeas, and roasted vegetables to bowl.
Add greens, cucumber, and microgreens.
Drizzle tahini-lemon dressing right before eating.
Top with pumpkin seeds.
meal_prep_notes: Store quinoa, chickpeas, greens, and dressing separately.
Chop cucumber 1–2 days at a time.
health_notes: Uses roasted vegetables as gut-friendlier base.

recipes.name: Mediterranean Roasted Vegetable Bowl
recipes.best_for: Monday dinner or light work lunch.
steps: Add quinoa/rice to bowl.
Warm roasted vegetables and chickpeas/tofu if desired.
Add greens, cucumber, and microgreens.
Drizzle tahini-lemon dressing.
Top with pumpkin seeds.
health_notes: Cooked vegetables make it more gut-friendly than all-raw salad.

recipes.name: Mexican Chana Rice Bowl
recipes.best_for: Sunday dinner or Tuesday lunch.
steps: Add rice and chana/chickpeas to bowl.
Add lettuce, cucumber, salsa, corn, and avocado.
Top with cilantro, lime/lemon, and pumpkin seeds.
Mix before eating.
meal_prep_notes: Use canned beans if dry beans were not soaked.
health_notes: Chana provides iron, protein, and fiber.
Raw lettuce/cucumber are toppings, not the whole meal.

recipes.name: Mexican Tofu Rice Bowl
recipes.best_for: Friday lunch or quick high-protein meal.
steps: Warm tofu with cumin, paprika, black pepper, and a few drops of water.
Add rice and tofu to bowl.
Add lettuce, cabbage, cucumber, salsa, corn, and avocado.
Finish with lime/lemon and cilantro.
meal_prep_notes: Keep tofu mildly seasoned during prep.
health_notes: Tofu provides vegetarian protein and iron.

recipes.name: Mixed Vegetable Curry using Pyaaz-Tamatar-Garlic Gravy
recipes.best_for: Using leftover gravy with cooked or roasted vegetables.
steps: Warm gravy in pan.
Add cooked/roasted vegetables.
Add water to adjust consistency.
Simmer 5–8 minutes.
Finish with kasuri methi and lemon if desired.
Serve with rice or roti.
meal_prep_notes: Use already-cooked vegetables for quick assembly.
Do not overcook if vegetables were already roasted.
health_notes: Good way to use cooked vegetables.
May be bloating-sensitive if onion/garlic gravy is used heavily.

recipes.name: Overnight Oats with Berries, Chia & Flaxseed
recipes.best_for: Fast workday breakfast.
steps: Add oats, chia, flaxseed, and cinnamon to jar.
Add soy milk and mix.
Refrigerate overnight.
Top with berries and nuts/seeds in morning.
health_notes: Berries are lower sugar than many fruits.

recipes.name: Overnight Oats with Kiwi, Chia & Flaxseed
recipes.best_for: Constipation-friendly fast breakfast.
steps: Add oats, chia, flaxseed, and cinnamon to jar.
Add soy milk and mix.
Refrigerate overnight.
Add chopped kiwi and seeds/nuts in the morning.

recipes.name: Paneer Curry using Pyaaz-Tamatar-Garlic Gravy
recipes.best_for: Occasional dairy-based variation only if tolerated.
steps: Warm gravy.
Add paneer cubes and a little water.
Simmer gently 3–5 minutes.
Finish with kasuri methi.
Serve with rice or roti.
meal_prep_notes: Keep paneer occasional because dairy may trigger acne.
Tofu is the default preferred protein.
health_notes: Not the default option for this plan due to dairy sensitivity.
Use only when truly wanted and observe skin response.

recipes.name: Pyaaz-Tamatar-Garlic Gravy Base
recipes.best_for: A flexible curry base for tofu, chana, mixed vegetables, bhindi, or occasional paneer.
steps: Heat oil and add cumin seeds.
Add onions and cook until soft and lightly golden.
Add ginger-garlic and cook until raw smell is gone.
Add tomatoes, turmeric, coriander powder, chili/paprika, hing, salt, and optional tomato paste.
Cook until tomatoes break down and mixture thickens.
Cool slightly and blend if a smooth gravy is desired.
Add kasuri methi at the end.
Store in small portions.
meal_prep_notes: Can refrigerate 3–4 days or freeze in small portions.
Do not make it too oily.
Make a lower onion/garlic version if bloating occurs.
health_notes: Useful but can be bloating-sensitive due to onion/garlic.
Best with tofu, mixed vegetables, or chickpeas.

recipes.name: Sambar Rice Bowl
recipes.best_for: Wednesday lunch or Saturday lunch.
steps: Warm rice and sambar separately.
Add rice to bowl and pour sambar over it.
Add bhindi/cabbage on side or top.
Add cucumber and microgreens after heating.
Add lemon if desired.
meal_prep_notes: Keep rice and sambar separate until eating.
health_notes: Toor dal sambar gives comfort and protein.

recipes.name: Sambar Rice Plate
recipes.best_for: Comfort dinner when wanting South Indian food.
steps: Warm rice, sambar, and side vegetable.
Serve rice with sambar over it or on the side.
Add bhindi/cabbage poriyal.
Add cucumber/microgreens.
Add small coconut chutney if eating with idli.
meal_prep_notes: Plate version is satisfying for dinner.
health_notes: Best with lauki, carrot, pumpkin, beans, and tomato in sambar.

recipes.name: Spinach Moong Dal Rice Bowl
recipes.best_for: Monday lunch or quick work lunch.
steps: Add rice to bowl.
Add spinach moong dal.
Add roasted vegetables.
Add cucumber and microgreens.
Squeeze lemon before eating.
Add pumpkin seeds if desired.
meal_prep_notes: Dal, rice, and vegetables keep 3–4 days.

recipes.name: Spinach Moong Dal Rice Plate
recipes.best_for: Saturday dinner or Tuesday dinner.
steps: Warm rice and spinach moong dal.
Warm roasted vegetables.
Place rice, dal, and vegetables on plate.
Add cucumber salad and microgreens.
Squeeze lemon over dal or salad.
meal_prep_notes: Plate version is best for dinner.
health_notes: Better for bloating than heavy rajma/chole meals.

recipes.name: Thai Peanut Tofu Rice Bowl
recipes.best_for: Wednesday dinner or Saturday lunch.
steps: Warm rice.
Warm tofu and broccoli.
Add rice to bowl.
Add tofu, broccoli, cabbage, carrot, and cucumber.
Drizzle peanut sauce.
Add herbs and crushed peanuts if using.

recipes.name: Tofu Curry Rice Bowl using Pyaaz-Tamatar-Garlic Gravy
recipes.best_for: Friday lunch or flexible curry meal.
steps: Warm gravy in a pan.
Add tofu cubes and a splash of water.
Simmer 5–8 minutes.
Add optional spinach/roasted vegetables.
Serve over rice with cucumber/microgreens.
Add lemon if desired.
meal_prep_notes: Keep tofu and gravy separate until assembling if possible.
Works well with frozen portions of gravy.
health_notes: Tofu is preferred over paneer for regular use.

recipes.name: Tofu Scramble Avocado Toast
recipes.best_for: Tuesday work-from-home breakfast.
steps: Press tofu lightly and crumble.
Heat oil and cook bell pepper and tomato.
Add spinach and wilt.
Add tofu, turmeric, cumin, pepper, and salt.
Cook 4–5 minutes.
Toast whole grain bread.
Mash avocado with lemon and salt.
Assemble toast with tofu scramble.
meal_prep_notes: Chopped vegetables can be prepped the night before.
Use whole grain bread, not white bread/maida bread.
